name: Russian

Avanesov, R. I. (1984). Russkoe literaturnoe proiznošenie. Moscow: Prosveščenie.

vowel_formants.speaker: adult male, single speaker, sustained isolated vowels

contrasts: palatalised ('soft') versus non-palatalised ('hard', slightly velarised) consonants at almost every place and manner, also word-finally and before consonants (брат [brat] vs брать [bratʲ], угол [ˈuɡəɫ] vs уголь [ˈuɡəlʲ])
unpaired hard /ʂ ʐ t͡s/ and unpaired soft /t͡ɕ ɕː j/; soft velars /kʲ ɡʲ xʲ/ are marginal
voiced versus voiceless obstruents (prevoiced versus voiceless unaspirated)
five stressed vowels /i e a o u/, with [ɨ] as a sixth phoneme or as the allophone of /i/ after hard consonants
position of stress is lexically contrastive (мука: [ˈmukə] 'torment' vs [mʊˈka] 'flour')
long /ɕː/ (and obsolescent /ʑː/) and geminates at morpheme boundaries
allophony: /i/ is [ɨ] after hard consonants, also across word boundaries (к Ивану [k ɨˈvanʊ]) and after ж ш ц whatever the spelling (жить [ʐɨtʲ])

stressed vowels are fronted and raised next to soft consonants: /a/ [æ] between soft consonants (пять [pʲætʲ]), /o/ [ɵ] (тётя [ˈtʲɵtʲə]), /u/ [ʉ] (люк), /e/ close [e] before soft and open [ɛ] after hard consonants
akanye: unstressed /o/ and /a/ merge after hard consonants, as [ɐ] in the syllable immediately before the stress and word-initially, as [ə] in other unstressed syllables (молоко [məɫɐˈko])
ikanye: unstressed /e/, /a/ and /o/ after soft consonants merge as [ɪ] (река [rʲɪˈka], пятно [pʲɪtˈno], часы [t͡ɕɪˈsɨ]); after hard ж ш ц unstressed /e/ is [ɨ̞] (жена [ʐɨˈna])
unstressed /u/ is [ʊ], unstressed /i/ is [ɪ] (after soft) or [ɨ̞] (after hard)

obstruent clusters take the voicing of their last member (regressive), also across the boundary with a proclitic (вокзал [vɐɡˈzaɫ], водка [ˈvotkə], к дому [ɡ ˈdomʊ], с братом [z ˈbratəm]); /v vʲ/ are devoiced but do not cause voicing
/t͡s t͡ɕ x/ have voiced allophones [d͡z d͡ʑ ɣ] before voiced obstruents
regressive assimilation of palatalisation in some clusters, chiefly dentals before soft dentals (степь [sʲtʲepʲ])
/ɡ/ is [x] before /k/ in лёгкий, мягкий and [v] in the endings -ого, -его; чт and чн are [ʂt], [ʂn] in что, конечно
/tʲ dʲ/ are slightly affricated [tˢʲ dᶻʲ]; /ɫ/ is dental and strongly velarised; /r/ is an apical trill or tap
cluster simplification in здравствуйте, солнце, сердце, поздно, лестница
phonotactics: onset clusters of up to four consonants (взгляд, встреча) and coda clusters of up to four (чёрств)
no voiced obstruents before a pause
only [ɪ ɨ̞ ʊ ə ɐ] occur in unstressed syllables
before /e/ in native words consonants are soft, except ж ш ц
single-consonant prepositions (в, к, с) form a syllable with the following word
no vowel hiatus restriction: sequences of vowels are allowed (поэт, наука)

stress.rule: Stress can fall on any syllable and may shift within a paradigm; it is not shown in ordinary spelling except by ё, which is always stressed.
stress.cues: duration and vowel quality (full versus reduced vowel) first, then intensity; pitch marks phrase accent rather than word stress

rhythm.vowel_reduction: strong: two degrees after hard consonants ([ɐ] in the first pretonic syllable, [ə] elsewhere) and merger to [ɪ] after soft consonants; unstressed vowels are short and can be devoiced or dropped in fast speech
rhythm.notes: The stressed syllable is the longest, the first pretonic syllable the next longest, other unstressed syllables shortest (Potebnja's pattern of relative prominence).

length.notes: No phonemic vowel length; stressed vowels are markedly longer than unstressed ones. Long consonants are /ɕː/, obsolescent /ʑː/ (now usually hard [ʐː]) and geminates at morpheme boundaries (ввоз, длинный, поддержать vs подержать); geminates are often shortened next to another consonant or far from the stress.

intonation.declarative: pre-nuclear stressed syllables carry rises or high plateaux; the nucleus (usually the last content word) has a fall that reaches low pitch on the stressed syllable, and later syllables stay low (IK-1)
intonation.yes_no_question: no change of word order and no final rise: a steep rise on the stressed syllable of the word in focus, peak at the end of that syllable, then low pitch on all following syllables (IK-3)
intonation.wh_question: high or falling accent with extra intensity on the question word or the nucleus, then falling to low (IK-2)
intonation.continuation: non-final phrases end in a rise on the last stressed syllable (IK-3), a fall-rise with the rise on post-tonic syllables (IK-4) or a high level (IK-6)
intonation.accent_shape: statement nucleus: fall completed within the stressed syllable; question nucleus: late-peaked rise within the stressed syllable followed by a low tail
intonation.notes: Bryzgunova's description uses seven intonation constructions (IK-1 to IK-7). The position of the pitch peak relative to the stressed syllable distinguishes question from statement.

tone.notes: No lexical tone or pitch accent.

problems: Soft labials, velars, /lʲ/ and /nʲ/ are coded as hard consonant plus a palatal glide phoneme [;] that is deleted when no vowel follows, so palatalisation is lost word-finally and before consonants: день, соль, уголь, степь, любовь, пальто, только come out hard (был and быль give identical audio). Only /tʲ dʲ sʲ zʲ mʲ/ and the sibilant series have their own soft phonemes; final рь is [r] plus a very short [ɪ].
Ikanye is applied only to the letter е: unstressed а, я after soft consonants and after ч, щ stay [a] or [ʌ] (пятно [pʲatˈno], часы [t͡ɕaˈsɨ], язык [jaˈzɨk], часовой) where the language has [ɪ].

Akanye is incomplete: unstressed о is [ʌ] (phoneme V) in every position including the first pretonic syllable, while pretonic а is [a], so pretonic /o/ and /a/ do not merge (вода [vʌˈda] vs сады [saˈdɨ]) and the two degrees [ɐ] and [ə] are not reproduced for о.

Stress comes from a large word list (ru_listx) and otherwise from a guess based on the number of syllables; unlisted or ambiguous forms get wrong stress and so wrong reduction (города is read горо́да).
No voicing assimilation between a preposition and its host: к дому, с братом, от брата keep voiceless [k s t], and из дома is devoiced to [ɪs].
Hard /ɫ/ uses a retroflex lateral (shown as ɭ in IPA output) and ы is shown as 'y'; stressed [æ] between soft consonants is not distinguished from [a].

Only the default eSpeak tunes are used: a question mark gives a fall-rise on the last stressed syllable for every question type, so the peak on the focused word of yes-no questions (IK-3) and the falling wh-question (IK-2) are missing.
солнце keeps [l] and бог ends in [k] (standard [ˈsont͡sə], [box]).

Vowel quality, from my own rough LPC measurement of the synthesiser output (not a published figure; F1/F2 in Hz): ы about 360/1680, у about 340/910, а about 910/1320, against Fant's 300/1480, 300/625 and 700/1080. So ы is fronter, у more central and а more open than the reference speaker; о (about 480/820) is close.
good: final devoicing and regressive voicing assimilation inside words (хлеб, вокзал, водка, сделать, отдать)
[ɨ] after hard consonants including жи, ши, ци, and unstressed е after ж ш ц as [ɨ] (жена, цена)
fronted vowels after soft consonants for о and у ([ɵ] in тётя, fronted u in люк)
exceptions что, конечно, его, сегодня and cluster simplification in здравствуйте, сердце, поздно, лестница
large stress dictionary; ё always stressed

notes: Formant values are those of Fant's single speaker and are close to cardinal citation vowels; running-speech vowels are more centralised. Chao-style tone data do not apply.
